co_school_room.blurb: School Room is the teaching corner of the Ouray Ice Park, in the Uncompahgre Gorge at roughly 7,900 feet. It was set up for newcomers to ice, and it still fills up on winter weekends. Most of the 16 lines are single pitches of about 60 to 100 feet: thirteen are water ice, mostly WI3 and WI4 with a couple at WI2 and one WI5, and three are mixed, from M5 to M7. Ice routes are normally protected with screws, and several are top-rope only. Because so many beginners gather here, falling ice is a real concern. The mixed lines are best early or late in the season, when rock shows between the ice sections.

co_f_garden_of_eden_wall.blurb: Garden of Eden Wall, also called the Pool Area, sits at the far end of Cascade Canyon north of Durango, at about 8,700 feet. You walk in past several other walls to reach the pool below the waterfall, which is a popular spot for a summer dip. The wall holds 16 climbs, nearly all of them sport, with most falling between 5.11 and 5.12 and a few easier lines in the 5.7 to 5.10 range. There is one trad route and a single hard boulder problem. The rock is limestone, and the setting is scenic, so expect company on warm days.

co_left_wall.blurb: Left Wall is the first cliff you meet when the trail reaches V Rock, near Pagosa Springs, and it has the shortest walk of any wall there. Its 16 climbs are almost all trad, with one sport route, and the grades run from the easy end of 5.7 through the 5.9s and 5.10s, up to a few 5.11 and 5.12 lines. The wall faces mostly south, so it bakes in summer. Fall is the better season, or come in late afternoon during hot months. Several lines are cracks and dihedrals that take a standard rack, and gear is generally good on the lower sections.
